summary: Checkout p99 tripled with no error-rate change and no deploy. Vigil named no culprit: the top candidate reached 0.35 confidence against a 0.4 floor. The brief carried three ranked candidates and the dashboard triage path, and the cause turned out to be the payments provider.

timeline.event: Checkout p99 begins drifting from its 780ms baseline.
First of three payment-path changes merges; two more follow within 40 minutes.
LatencyBudgetBurn alert fired for checkout (p99 2.4s, budget burning 6x).
Vigil brief posted: no culprit named, three candidates ranked with rationales, dashboards runbook cited.
Incident marked resolved after authorization traffic failed over to the secondary region.

root_cause: The payments provider's authorization latency rose roughly 900ms over three hours. Checkout p99 tracked it directly. The three code changes in the window were coincidental: the drift predates all of them and a replay against the previous build reproduces the same p99.
contributing_factors: Provider-side latency had no panel of its own, so gateway time and service time could not be separated at a glance.
Three payment-path changes landed inside the alert window and drew initial suspicion.
impact: No requests failed; checkout p99 ran at 2.4s against a 780ms baseline, burning the latency budget roughly 6x for the duration.
resolution: Failed authorization traffic over to the provider's secondary region, which returned p99 to 900ms. The provider confirmed a regional capacity issue on their side.
went_well: The confidence floor prevented an innocent commit from being recorded as the cause of a provider outage.
On-call still received ranked candidates with per-feature scores and the rationale for dismissing each.
went_poorly: Three hours of drift passed before the budget-burn alert paged anyone.
Nothing alerts on the payments provider's own latency, so the actual cause had to be found by hand.

action_items.description: Add an SLO alert on payments provider authorization latency.
Split gateway time from service time on the Checkout Overview dashboard.
Document the secondary-region failover in the checkout runbook.
